Dr. Richard Chumney

The American Tobacco Co.
P. O. Box 799

Hopewell, Virginia 23860

Dear Dick;

I am sending you another package via air freight containing two bobbins of cigarette paper. One of these (898-69) is a candidate designed to match the performance of our competitor's paper that you are currently using on PALL MALL BENTHOL 100\( ^{1} \)'s. The bobbin was made by electrically perforating to 100 cm/min a base paper having an inherent porosity of 45 cm/min and a citrate level of 0.8 % (as citric acid). This should provide the required reduction in the delivery of particulate matter. Should the sample not be quite on the mark, let me know and we'll make whatever changes are necessary.

We prepared the other enclosed bobbin (883-21-5) in response to the very clear impression we received from your group when we visited you regarding your interest in reducing the delivery of carbon monoxide relative to that of particulate matter. We spoke to you at that time of the nearly optimal benefit obtained by using paper which is treated with very low levels of citrate. To this end we prepared some paper at 40 cm/min but having 0.43% citrate applied to it. You will find that this paper will give a marked reduction in the ratio of carbon monoxide to tar compared to, say, our regular 110-6. In fact, you might want to compare 883-21-5 with one of the bobbins described in my letter to you of May 3, No. 883-21-1; the latter is merely a lab-made version of 110-6.

Please let me know if your data support our convictions regarding the influence of the burn chemical or if you'd like to see additional paper at this or any other permeability which would be embodiments of the same concept.

Very truly yours,

[SIGNATURE] Culii

C. F. Mattina
Research Department
